questions.knowledge_point: Determining the Dimension of the Null Space of a Matrix Given the Number of Non-Pivot Columns
questions.problem: Let $W$ be a $9\times 10$ matrix that has $8$ pivot columns. What is the dimension of the null space of $W?$
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $\text{dim(Null}(W))$ is the number of non-pivot columns in $W.$ 

Since $W$ has $10$ columns and $8$ of them are pivots, then the number of non-pivot columns in $W$ is 

$$
10-8=2.
$$

Therefore, $\text{dim(Null}(W))=2.$

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Dimension of the Null Space of Matrices Using Inspection
questions.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

- If $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(A))=0.$
- If $B=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(B))=2.$
- If $C=[\begin{aligned}5 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]$ then $\text{dim(Null}(C))=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
The dimension of the null space of a matrix is the number of non-pivot columns in the matrix. 

Also, all of the given matrices are in row echelon form.

With that in mind, let's consider each of the statements.

- Statement I is true. The matrix $A$ has $2$ pivot columns and no non-pivot columns. So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(A))=0.
$$

- Statement II is false. The matrix $B$ has $2$ pivot column and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $3$rd column). So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(B))=1.
$$

- Statement III is true. The matrix $C$ has $2$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $2$nd column). So, 

$$
\text{dim(Null}(C))=1.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Nullity of a Matrix Using Row Reduction
questions.worked_solution:
To find $\text{dim}(\text{Null}(A))$, we reduce $A$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 2 & 0 \\ 8 & 0 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & -4 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+(-\frac{1}{2}){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix has $3$ pivot columns and $1$ non-pivot column (namely, the $4$th column). 

Therefore,

$$
\text{dim}(\text{Null}(A))=1.
$$

Recall that by definition, $\text{nullity}(D)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(D)).$

To find $\text{dim}(\text{Null}(D))$, we reduce $D$ to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}D & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 5 & -7 & 9 \\ -3 & 6 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 \\ -3 & 6 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 9 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix has $3$ pivot columns and no non-pivot columns. 

Therefore,

$$
\text{nullity}(D)=\text{dim}(\text{Null}(D))=0.
$$
